brewing.notes: A safe starting point for raw pu-erh: rinse once, gongfu style, short early steeps.

description:
A bamboo-shaped tea from Diwei Township in Guangnan County, Yunnan, made by packing tea with glutinous rice into golden bamboo. It is a traditional speciality of the local Zhuang.

Treat it as you would any raw pu-erh: rinse the leaf, keep early steeps short, and ask which year and which trees it comes from, since village names on Yunnan teas are often stretched.
history: Its making is said to go back more than 300 years, and one Yang Chunji of Diwei is credited with the bamboo and rice method in 1862. By tradition a girl gave it to her sweetheart as a token, hence the name Guniang Cha, or girl's tea. Production was revived and enlarged in 1990, and it is counted among Yunnan's ten fine teas.
processing: Tea and glutinous rice are packed into golden bamboo and first dried on a rack, so that moisture moves outward and the scents of tea, bamboo and rice come through; several further steps with added ingredients follow.
harvest_season: Usually spring leaf is prized, as with most raw pu-erh.
appearance_dry: Bamboo-tube shape, tightly packed inside, with tender buds and plenty of white down.
taste_profile: Strongly aromatic, fresh and sweet, with a long finish.
vintage_note: Raw pu-erh is sold by harvest year: young at 1 to 3 years, mid-aged at 5 to 10, aged at 15 or more. Storage matters as much as age.
